thread:
Anya: flagging a customer ticket — their p99 for API calls from apac-region jumped ~3x around 10:12 UTC, traces show long TLS handshake times and extra hop. raising here to see if anyone sees a routing pattern :eyes:
Mike: saw the alert too. I can repro from our apac probe. TLS handshake timeouts/extra RTT between our edge and customer client IPs.
Tariq: can you paste the probe curl/traceroute? also which POPs see it?
Anya: paste: ```curl -v --resolve api.redwood.local:443:34.123.45.67 https://api.redwood.local/health``` output: `* Connected to 34.123.45.67 (34.123.45.67) port 443 # TCP handshake ok
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Client hello (1) 
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Server hello (2) 
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Encrypted Extensions (8) 
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Certificate (11) 
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, CertificateVerify (15) 
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Finished (20) 
* TLS handshake took 582 ms```
Lindsey: 582ms is massive for handshake. What do TCP/route hops show?
Mike: traceroute (apac-probe -> edge): `1 10.0.0.1 1.2ms; 2 203.0.113.4 8ms; 3 198.51.100.7 120ms; 4 198.51.100.8 118ms; 5 34.123.45.67 2ms` — note hop 3/4 spike then back to normal at endpoint. Looks like an intermediate AS path detour.
Tariq: that smells like a route-slew or partial announcement change at a transit. Might cause extra cross-zone bouncing before hitting our POP. Do we have BGP/peering telemetry for that time?
Anya: ops-bot posted routing-change alert at 10:08: `bgp: AS64512 withdrew prefix 34.123.45.0/24 then re-announced via peer 203:110` — attaching snippet.
Mike: also saw an increase in TLS renegotiation on that POP. Could be SNI mismatch causing fallback to different backend. Any recent rollout that could change SNI handling?
Lindsey: no SNI code changes in last 24h. But we pushed a small egress policy tweak to the POP yesterday that alters preferred egress peer order. Could interact with transit behavior.
Tariq: mitigation ideas: 1) force route preference to non-flapping peer for affected POP (hotfix AS-path prepend), 2) fail traffic to EU-pop based on client geo for this customer, 3) temp increase TLS handshake timeout/retry to hide transient handshakes while route stabilizes.
Anya: customer requests quick mitigation. I can patch traffic policy to prefer peer-A for their CIDR. Mike, can you run a canary policy?
Mike: on it. Applying policy: `egress-policy apply --pop apac-pop-3 --prefer-peer peer-A --match client_cidr 203.0.113.0/24 --dry-run` then `--commit`. Will monitor p99.
Lindsey: also enabling a short-term `tls-resumption` force (enable session tickets) on that POP to reduce full-handshakes if we see retries. Ops: is that safe?
Tariq: session tickets are enabled cluster-wide but some clients/peers drop resumption. Worth enabling aggressive resumption cache for that POP; risk minimal.
ops-bot: audit log: egress-policy commit by Mike at 10:22 UTC, policy id ep-339-01.
Mike: after policy change p99 dropped from 1.8s -> 420ms within two minutes for the customer IPs. Handshake times down to ~90ms.
Anya: customer emailed confirming latency improved. Leaving here for postmortem notes.
Lindsey: next steps for RCA: 1) correlate peering change (AS64512) with our peer ordering tweak, 2) check transit provider logs for the short announcement/AS-path shift, 3) consider automated peer-failover when intermediate hop latency exceeds threshold.
Tariq: add a probe that watches hop delta (pre-pop vs intermediate) and triggers auto-route-prefer when delta > 100ms for N minutes. Will draft RFC.
Anya: I'll file the support escalation follow-up to the account ticket with a summary + mitigation steps.
support-agent: filing note: ticket #CUST-4521 updated with mitigation timeline and policy id ep-339-01. Customer ops notified.
Lindsey: marking thread resolved for customer impact; keep monitoring for 2 hours then close. :white_check_mark:
